Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: There is no explicit marker for the absolutive case.
curated_comment: Ku Waru (boun1245, Trans-New Guinea, Papua New Guinea) shows ergative alignment documented in Merlan and Rumsey (1991). The ergative marker is -n(i) (optionally reduced to -n). All 24 features verified against Merlan and Rumsey (1991). Key updates from original annotation: GB409_16 changed '?'→1 and GB409_17 changed '?'→1. No topicality-based split is documented; the optional marker drop is phonologically/discourse conditioned. GB409_15=1 confirmed via Type IV clause constructions (p.339: experiencer arguments with hunger-ERG, sleep-ERG). GB409_22=1 confirmed: five-way clause type distinction constitutes additional conditioning. Glottocode boun1245 is correct; the previously proposed kuwa1244 does not exist in Glottolog.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: In the context of an agentive A argument, ergative alignment is observed.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: In the context of a non-agentive A, ergative alignment is observed. Merlan and Rumsey (1991: 339) document Type IV clause constructions where experiencer-like arguments (e.g., 'hunger-ERG', 'sleep-ERG') take the ergative marker.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No topicality-based split is documented in Merlan and Rumsey (1991). The optional dropping of -n(i) is conditioned by phonological/discourse factors, not by the topicality of A per se. Topical A retains ergative marking. Changed from original annotation '?' to 1.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: No topicality-based split documented. Non-topical A takes ergative marking as expected. Changed from original annotation '?' to 1.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Clauses with animate A arguments exhibit ergative alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Clauses with inanimate A arguments exhibit ergative alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: Main clauses exhibit ergative alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Non-main clauses exhibit ergative alignment.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Ergative marking is conditioned by a split intransitivity system based on control of the S argument (five clause types distinguished in Ku Waru), not purely topicality or animacy.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The ergative marker does not have the same form as the genitive marker.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: The ergative marker -n(i) is also used as the instrumental marker. Comitative uses a different form. ERG=INST confirmed.
